content.what_it_is: MATLAB extractor that loads seven eta snapshots and takes each snapshot's second row (lines 2-20), builds a normalized descending spatial coordinate from the first file's length (lines 25-28), selects samples with normalized x between -2 and 20 and stores seven normalized elevations (lines 30-45), reconstructs corresponding coordinates in column 1 (lines 46-50), and writes an eight-column tab-delimited FUNWAVE_BP1_SHAPE.txt file (line 52).

params_defined.name: dx
params_defined.range: positive for assumed monotonic coordinate selection

equations.ref: first snapshot normalized elevation; columns 3-8 repeat for d2-d7
coordinate reconstruction for reverse-ordered selected rows

io.name: FUNWAVE_BP1_SHAPE.txt as tab-delimited data with precision 6

unresolved: Cross-file range coupling: n is computed only from eta_0112 on line 7 and then used to index d1 through d7 together on lines 31-42. Later snapshots are never checked for equal second-row lengths, so any shorter row causes out-of-range access and any longer row is silently truncated.

Shape/interface defect: every load is assumed to return a matrix with at least two rows (lines 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20), while n=length(d) on line 7 returns the largest matrix dimension rather than the second-row width. If a snapshot has more rows than columns, the loop bound can exceed d1's length.

Empty-selection use-before-assign: data and kk are created only when a coordinate passes both tests on lines 32-35. If no sample lies in [-2,20], the coordinate loop is empty but line 52 still writes undefined data.

The coordinate reconstruction on line 49 depends on accepted indices forming one contiguous run and on kk retaining the smallest accepted index from the reverse scan. That holds only because the hard-coded dx is positive and the current x formula is monotone; this invariant is not checked if parameters change.

All seven loads and the output write are unchecked, and fdir defaults to the process working directory, so missing/malformed snapshots or an unwritable output path fail without a controlled diagnostic.
